claims.title: The Sumerians invent cuneiform writing
claims.summary: In the Sumerian city of Uruk, scribes develop cuneiform — wedge-shaped marks pressed into clay — first to keep accounts and then to record law, literature and history, making Mesopotamia the cradle of the written word.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iraq: From the first cities of Sumer to the modern republic on the Tigris and Euphrates.", terralore.co/country/IRQ/chronicle#ev-3200bce-the-sumerians-invent-cuneiform-writing, claim TL:IRQ:event:3200bce:the-sumerians-invent-cuneiform-writing, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Sargon founds the Akkadian Empire
claims.summary: Sargon of Akkad unites the Sumerian city-states under one ruler, creating what is often called history's first empire, with its capital at Akkad and a Semitic-speaking dynasty.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iraq: From the first cities of Sumer to the modern republic on the Tigris and Euphrates.", terralore.co/country/IRQ/chronicle#ev-2334bce-sargon-founds-the-akkadian-empire, claim TL:IRQ:event:2334bce:sargon-founds-the-akkadian-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Hammurabi issues his law code
claims.summary: Hammurabi, sixth king of Babylon, unifies much of Mesopotamia and promulgates the Code of Hammurabi, 282 laws inscribed on a diorite stela — one of the most complete legal collections of the ancient world.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iraq: From the first cities of Sumer to the modern republic on the Tigris and Euphrates.", terralore.co/country/IRQ/chronicle#ev-1755bce-hammurabi-issues-his-law-code, claim TL:IRQ:event:1755bce:hammurabi-issues-his-law-code, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fall of Nineveh and the Assyrian Empire
claims.summary: A coalition of Babylonians and Medes besieges and destroys Nineveh, capital of the Neo-Assyrian Empire whose first capital, Ashur, is now a UNESCO World Heritage site, ending Assyrian power and clearing the way for the Neo-Babylonian Empire.

sources.label: Ashur (Qal'at Sherqat) — UNESCO World Heritage List

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iraq: From the first cities of Sumer to the modern republic on the Tigris and Euphrates.", terralore.co/country/IRQ/chronicle#ev-612bce-fall-of-nineveh-and-the-assyrian-empire, claim TL:IRQ:event:612bce:fall-of-nineveh-and-the-assyrian-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Babylon at its height under Nebuchadnezzar II
claims.summary: The Neo-Babylonian Empire reaches its zenith under Nebuchadnezzar II, who rebuilds Babylon with the Ishtar Gate and great walls; the ruined city, associated with the Hanging Gardens, is today a UNESCO World Heritage site.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iraq: From the first cities of Sumer to the modern republic on the Tigris and Euphrates.", terralore.co/country/IRQ/chronicle#ev-575bce-babylon-at-its-height-under-nebuchadnezzar-ii, claim TL:IRQ:event:575bce:babylon-at-its-height-under-nebuchadnezzar-ii, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Cyrus the Great captures Babylon
claims.summary: The Persian king Cyrus the Great takes Babylon, ending the Neo-Babylonian Empire and bringing Mesopotamia into the Achaemenid Persian realm as one of its richest provinces.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iraq: From the first cities of Sumer to the modern republic on the Tigris and Euphrates.", terralore.co/country/IRQ/chronicle#ev-539bce-cyrus-the-great-captures-babylon, claim TL:IRQ:event:539bce:cyrus-the-great-captures-babylon, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Hatra, capital of an Arab kingdom
claims.summary: Under Parthian influence the fortified city of Hatra flourishes as the capital of a small Arab kingdom, twice withstanding Roman sieges before falling in the 3rd century; its ruins are now a UNESCO World Heritage site.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iraq: From the first cities of Sumer to the modern republic on the Tigris and Euphrates.", terralore.co/country/IRQ/chronicle#ev-100-hatra-capital-of-an-arab-kingdom, claim TL:IRQ:event:100:hatra-capital-of-an-arab-kingdom, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mesopotamia under the Sasanians
claims.summary: The Sasanian dynasty replaces the Parthians and rules Mesopotamia from Ctesiphon, making the fertile 'Sawad' the agricultural and administrative core of the Sasanian Empire for four centuries.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iraq: From the first cities of Sumer to the modern republic on the Tigris and Euphrates.", terralore.co/country/IRQ/chronicle#ev-224-mesopotamia-under-the-sasanians, claim TL:IRQ:event:224:mesopotamia-under-the-sasanians, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of al-Qadisiyyah and the Arab conquest
claims.summary: Arab Muslim armies of the Rashidun Caliphate defeat the Sasanians at al-Qadisiyyah near al-Hira and take Ctesiphon, ending Persian rule in Mesopotamia and beginning the region's Islamisation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iraq: From the first cities of Sumer to the modern republic on the Tigris and Euphrates.", terralore.co/country/IRQ/chronicle#ev-636-battle-of-al-qadisiyyah-and-the-arab-conquest, claim TL:IRQ:event:636:battle-of-al-qadisiyyah-and-the-arab-conquest, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Al-Mansur founds Baghdad
claims.summary: The Abbasid caliph al-Mansur founds Baghdad on the Tigris as his 'City of Peace', a circular capital that swiftly becomes one of the world's largest and wealthiest cities.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iraq: From the first cities of Sumer to the modern republic on the Tigris and Euphrates.", terralore.co/country/IRQ/chronicle#ev-762-al-mansur-founds-baghdad, claim TL:IRQ:event:762:al-mansur-founds-baghdad, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The House of Wisdom and the Golden Age
claims.summary: Under Harun al-Rashid and al-Ma'mun, Baghdad's scholars — associated with the Bayt al-Hikmah, the 'House of Wisdom' — translate and advance Greek, Persian and Indian learning during the Islamic Golden Age.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iraq: From the first cities of Sumer to the modern republic on the Tigris and Euphrates.", terralore.co/country/IRQ/chronicle#ev-800-the-house-of-wisdom-and-the-golden-age, claim TL:IRQ:event:800:the-house-of-wisdom-and-the-golden-age, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Samarra becomes the Abbasid capital
claims.summary: The caliphs move their capital upriver to Samarra, building immense palaces and the Great Mosque with its spiral Malwiya minaret, today a UNESCO World Heritage site.

sources.label: Samarra Archaeological City — UNESCO World Heritage List

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iraq: From the first cities of Sumer to the modern republic on the Tigris and Euphrates.", terralore.co/country/IRQ/chronicle#ev-836-samarra-becomes-the-abbasid-capital, claim TL:IRQ:event:836:samarra-becomes-the-abbasid-capital, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Mongol sack of Baghdad
claims.summary: The Mongol forces of Hulagu Khan besiege and storm Baghdad, executing the last Abbasid caliph al-Musta'sim and destroying the city; the sack ends the Abbasid Caliphate and devastates the region.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iraq: From the first cities of Sumer to the modern republic on the Tigris and Euphrates.", terralore.co/country/IRQ/chronicle#ev-1258-the-mongol-sack-of-baghdad, claim TL:IRQ:event:1258:the-mongol-sack-of-baghdad, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ottoman conquest of Baghdad
claims.summary: The Ottoman Empire takes definitive control of Baghdad from Safavid Persia, ruling Mesopotamia for nearly three centuries as the provinces of Mosul, Baghdad and Basra.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iraq: From the first cities of Sumer to the modern republic on the Tigris and Euphrates.", terralore.co/country/IRQ/chronicle#ev-1638-ottoman-conquest-of-baghdad, claim TL:IRQ:event:1638:ottoman-conquest-of-baghdad, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: British mandate and the Iraqi revolt
claims.summary: After capturing Baghdad in 1917, Britain is granted a League of Nations mandate over Iraq; a widespread anti-British revolt in 1920 pushes Britain toward installing an Arab monarchy.

sources.label: Iraq — British occupation and the mandatory regime

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iraq: From the first cities of Sumer to the modern republic on the Tigris and Euphrates.", terralore.co/country/IRQ/chronicle#ev-1920-british-mandate-and-the-iraqi-revolt, claim TL:IRQ:event:1920:british-mandate-and-the-iraqi-revolt, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Faisal I crowned king of Iraq
claims.summary: Britain installs the Hashemite prince Faisal I, a leader of the wartime Arab Revolt, as king of the new Iraqi state, creating a monarchy and parliament under British supervision.

sources.label: Iraq — British occupation and the mandatory regime

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iraq: From the first cities of Sumer to the modern republic on the Tigris and Euphrates.", terralore.co/country/IRQ/chronicle#ev-1921-faisal-i-crowned-king-of-iraq, claim TL:IRQ:event:1921:faisal-i-crowned-king-of-iraq, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence and entry into the League of Nations
claims.summary: The British mandate ends and the Kingdom of Iraq is admitted to the League of Nations as an independent state — the first League mandate anywhere to achieve independence.

sources.label: A Guide to the History of Recognition: Iraq
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iraq: From the first cities of Sumer to the modern republic on the Tigris and Euphrates.", terralore.co/country/IRQ/chronicle#ev-1932-independence-and-entry-into-the-league-of, claim TL:IRQ:event:1932:independence-and-entry-into-the-league-of, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Republican coup ends the monarchy
claims.summary: Army officers led by Abd al-Karim Qasim overthrow the Hashemite monarchy in a predawn coup; King Faisal II is killed and the Republic of Iraq is proclaimed.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iraq: From the first cities of Sumer to the modern republic on the Tigris and Euphrates.", terralore.co/country/IRQ/chronicle#ev-1958-republican-coup-ends-the-monarchy, claim TL:IRQ:event:1958:republican-coup-ends-the-monarchy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Saddam Hussein assumes the presidency
claims.summary: After years consolidating power within the Ba'ath Party, Saddam Hussein formally becomes president of Iraq in July 1979 and establishes a brutal one-man dictatorship.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iraq: From the first cities of Sumer to the modern republic on the Tigris and Euphrates.", terralore.co/country/IRQ/chronicle#ev-1979-saddam-hussein-assumes-the-presidency, claim TL:IRQ:event:1979:saddam-hussein-assumes-the-presidency, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Iran–Iraq War
claims.summary: Iraq invades Iran in September 1980, beginning an eight-year war of attrition that kills an estimated several hundred thousand to over a million people on both sides before a UN-mediated ceasefire takes effect in 1988.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iraq: From the first cities of Sumer to the modern republic on the Tigris and Euphrates.", terralore.co/country/IRQ/chronicle#ev-1980-the-iran-iraq-war, claim TL:IRQ:event:1980:the-iran-iraq-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Invasion of Kuwait and the Persian Gulf War
claims.summary: Iraq invades and annexes Kuwait in August 1990; a United States-led coalition of many nations expels Iraqi forces in early 1991, after which Iraq is placed under severe international sanctions.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iraq: From the first cities of Sumer to the modern republic on the Tigris and Euphrates.", terralore.co/country/IRQ/chronicle#ev-1991-invasion-of-kuwait-and-the-persian-gulf-war, claim TL:IRQ:event:1991:invasion-of-kuwait-and-the-persian-gulf-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: US-led invasion topples Saddam Hussein
claims.summary: A United States-led coalition invades Iraq and overthrows Saddam Hussein's government within weeks; Saddam is captured in December 2003 and later executed in 2006.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iraq: From the first cities of Sumer to the modern republic on the Tigris and Euphrates.", terralore.co/country/IRQ/chronicle#ev-2003-us-led-invasion-topples-saddam-hussein, claim TL:IRQ:event:2003:us-led-invasion-topples-saddam-hussein, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: New constitution and sectarian war
claims.summary: Iraq adopts a federal, power-sharing constitution, but a Sunni-led insurgency and, after the 2006 al-Askari shrine bombing, brutal Shiʿi–Sunni sectarian violence engulf the country.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iraq: From the first cities of Sumer to the modern republic on the Tigris and Euphrates.", terralore.co/country/IRQ/chronicle#ev-2005-new-constitution-and-sectarian-war, claim TL:IRQ:event:2005:new-constitution-and-sectarian-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: ISIS seizes Mosul and proclaims a caliphate
claims.summary: The jihadist group ISIS sweeps across northern Iraq, captures Mosul, and declares a 'caliphate', imposing extreme violence and destroying heritage sites including parts of Hatra, Ashur and Nimrud.

sources.label: Islamic State in Iraq and the Levant (ISIS)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iraq: From the first cities of Sumer to the modern republic on the Tigris and Euphrates.", terralore.co/country/IRQ/chronicle#ev-2014-isis-seizes-mosul-and-proclaims-a-caliphate, claim TL:IRQ:event:2014:isis-seizes-mosul-and-proclaims-a-caliphate, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Liberation of Mosul and defeat of ISIS
claims.summary: Backed by a US-led coalition, Iraqi forces retake Mosul in July 2017 after months of urban warfare, and Iraq declares victory over ISIS in December 2017, ending its territorial control.

sources.label: Islamic State in Iraq and the Levant (ISIS)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iraq: From the first cities of Sumer to the modern republic on the Tigris and Euphrates.", terralore.co/country/IRQ/chronicle#ev-2017-liberation-of-mosul-and-defeat-of-isis, claim TL:IRQ:event:2017:liberation-of-mosul-and-defeat-of-isis, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
